paper_title: Strong constraints on decay and annihilation of dark matter from heating of gas-rich dwarf galaxies
notes: Paper (Wadekar & Wang, arXiv:2111.08025) derives new bounds on DM decay/annihilation from gas heating of the Leo T dwarf galaxy, and recasts the chi->gamma-gamma decay lifetime bound into the ALP-photon coupling g_agamma (Fig. 4), stated to be the strongest limit for ma ~ 30 eV - 1 keV (valid above ~26.2 eV where decay photons exceed the H ionization threshold). Exact numerical curve values are in figures/GitHub data files not reproduced in the text; the data_points above were reconstructed from the paper's stated cooling rate (7e-30 GeV cm^-3 s^-1), the Leo T DM density profile, the opacity curve description, and Gamma_a = m_a^3 g^2/(64 pi), so they are approximate (factor ~2-3 uncertainty). This is an astrophysical DM-decay bound (assumes ALPs are all of the halo DM in Leo T), not a haloscope, so no local DM density is set. No formal confidence level is quoted (bound is heating < cooling); 0.95 entered as placeholder. The paper also constrains Higgs-portal scalars, sterile neutrinos, and dark baryons, but the AxionPhoton result is the relevant enum match. | selector: text over figure_vision (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0.45, 8))
